items.prompt: You already know how the rook and the bishop move. Before any explanation, tap every square you think this white queen can reach. The kings are only on the board because a position needs both.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the queen on d4 can move to.

hints: Try each direction from d4 in turn.
Straight along the d-file and the fourth rank, and slanting along both diagonals.
Think of the rook's squares and the bishop's squares, both from d4. Then go all the way to the edge in all eight directions.
items.explain: The queen reaches 27 squares: 14 along the d-file and the fourth rank, like a rook, and 13 along the two diagonals, like a bishop. No piece stands on any of her lines.

items.prompt: Same piece, new square. Tap every square the white queen on a1 can reach.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the queen on a1 can move to.

hints: From a corner she has only three lines instead of eight.
One line goes up the a-file, one along the first rank, one along the long diagonal.
Seven squares on each of the three lines, to the edge.
items.explain: From the corner she has 21 squares: seven up the a-file, seven along the first rank and seven along the long diagonal. That is fewer than the 27 she has in the middle, because five of her eight lines point off the board.

items.prompt: Can the white queen on d4 reach e6 in one move? (e6 is a knight-shaped hop away: two squares one way, one the other.) Predict, then check.

claims.statement: e6 is not on any rank, file or diagonal through d4, so the queen cannot go there.
e5 is one step up the diagonal, and it is allowed.

hints: Check each of her eight lines in turn.
e6 is one file to the right and two ranks up.
e6 is one file over and two ranks up: is that on any of her eight lines?
items.explain: e6 is one file over and two ranks up, which lies on none of her lines. The queen never makes that knight-shaped hop. She can reach e5, which is one step along the diagonal.

items.prompt: Can the white queen on a1 take the black pawn on a5 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The a-file between a1 and a5 is empty, so the queen can take the pawn.
The pawn on b2 does block the long diagonal.

hints: Look at what stands on each of her lines.
Which line leads from a1 to a5, and is anything on it?
a5 is on the a-file, which is a different line.
items.explain: The pawn on b2 shuts the long diagonal, but a5 is on the a-file and the squares a2 to a4 are empty. Each line is blocked on its own, so the queen takes the pawn.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white queen on d4 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the queen on d4 can move to.

hints: Three white pawns stand right next to her. Which lines do they shut?
The pawns on c4, e4 and d3 close the left, the right and the down lines completely.
Two black pawns, on b2 and f6, are the ends of two diagonals: she can take them but not pass.
items.explain: Up the d-file she has d5 to d8, four squares. The four diagonals give ten more, counting the captures on b2 and f6. Four plus ten makes 14.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white queen on e4 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the queen on e4 can move to.

hints: Take the eight directions one at a time.
Which of her lines is shut at once by her own pawn?
A line ends before her own piece and on an enemy piece.
items.explain: Her own pawn on f3 shuts the line down to the right, and the black pawn on c6 ends the line up to the left (she may take it). Every other line runs to the board's edge. That makes 22 squares.

items.prompt: Tap every square the white queen on f2 can move to.

claims.statement: These are exactly the squares the queen on f2 can move to.

hints: Check each of the eight directions in turn.
Your own pawn shuts one line; an enemy pawn ends another.
She stops in front of her own pieces and may take an enemy piece.
items.explain: Her own pawn on b2 stops the queen on c2 along the second rank, and the black pawn on c5 ends the diagonal after e3 and d4 (she may take it on c5). The other lines run to the edge. That makes 19 squares.

items.prompt: Capture a black pawn with the white queen.

claims.statement: The queen can capture the pawn on b6.
The queen cannot capture the pawn on f7.

hints: Which pawn stands on one of her eight lines?
Is the other pawn on a row, a column or a diagonal through d4?
Check the squares between the queen and the pawn.
items.explain: The pawn on b6 is on the diagonal d4, c5, b6 with c5 empty. The pawn on f7 is two files over and three ranks up from d4, which is on none of her lines.

items.prompt: The white queen is on c1 and a black rook is on h6. Can the queen take the rook in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The queen can capture the rook on h6.

hints: Is h6 on one of her lines from c1?
Count the diagonal squares from c1: d2, e3, f4, g5, h6. Is anything on them?
An enemy piece at the end of a clear line can be taken.
items.explain: h6 is on the long diagonal from c1, and d2, e3, f4 and g5 are empty. The queen slides the whole way and takes the rook.

items.prompt: The white queen is on a4, her own pawn on c6 and a black pawn on d7. Can the queen take the pawn on d7 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The queen cannot move from a4 to d7.
The queen can move one step along the same diagonal, to b5.

hints: Which line leads from a4 towards d7?
Which squares lie on it, and who stands on them?
The queen cannot jump over her own pawn.
items.explain: d7 is on the diagonal a4, b5, c6, d7, but her own pawn stands on c6. She can reach b5 and no further on that line, so d7 is out of reach this move.

items.prompt: The white queen is on d1 with her own pawn on d2, and a black pawn stands on h5. Can the queen take the pawn on h5 in one move? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: The queen can capture the pawn on h5.
The queen cannot go up the d-file past her own pawn.

hints: Which line leads from d1 to h5?
The pawn on d2 shuts one line only. Is it the line to h5?
The diagonal d1, e2, f3, g4, h5 is a different line from the d-file.
items.explain: The pawn on d2 shuts the d-file, but the diagonal d1, e2, f3, g4, h5 is empty. The queen slides along it and takes the pawn.

items.prompt: Count the squares each white piece can move to. Which piece has more squares to choose from, the queen on c3 or the rook on f5?

claims.statement: The queen on c3 can move to 25 squares.
The rook on f5 can move to 14 squares.

hints: Count one piece at a time, one direction at a time.
The rook has four lines, the queen eight.
Count carefully: the rook's squares are all on the f-file and the fifth rank.
items.explain: The queen on c3 can move to 25 squares and the rook on f5 to 14. The queen has the diagonals as well as the rows and columns, which is why she has more here.
